table.$comment: A table the consumer writes, dressed element by element: the table, its caption, header cells, cells and the frame it scrolls in. It stands on no control axis, because a cell is not a control: the padding comes off the spacing scale, so the density scope tightens a table with everything else, and the type is the body size. The only colours of its own are the header's surface and the lines: the cells paint nothing, so a table sits on whatever surface holds it.
table.$comment-padding: `space.3` and `space.4`, the two steps the compact density re-points, so a dense page gets dense rows without a table input of its own.

padding-y.$description: Vertical padding of a cell and a header cell.

padding-x.$description: Horizontal padding of a cell and a header cell.

heading-fg.$description: Text colour of a header cell.

heading-font-weight.$description: Font weight of a header cell.

caption-gap.$description: Space between the caption and the table.

toggle-gap.$description: Gap between a sortable header's label and its chevron.

table.$comment-toggle-target-min: The floor a finger gets on a sortable header (`req-a11y-touch`). The cell's padding clears it at the body size; this is what a skin that shrinks the padding runs into.

toggle-target-min.$description: Touch-target floor of a sortable header.

table.$comment-icon-fg-muted: The chevron of a column not yet sorted, shown under the pointer or the focus as the order a press would give. The muted text colour, so the hint reads quieter than the sorted column's chevron, which takes the header's own text colour.

icon-fg-muted.$description: Colour of the chevron a sortable header shows as a hint.

table.$comment-rows: The data table's surfaces, which the first layer has no row of its own for (0096 dressed no `<tr>`). A row's surface is one of three — its tone, the pointer's tint, the stripe — and the stripe is the header's own surface, so a striped table reads as one surface with every other row lifted. The pointer takes the primary's second fill: not the stripe's, or a striped row under the pointer would show nothing, and not the first, which is the info tone's colour in both themes.

bg-hover.$description: Background of a data table's row under the pointer.

bg-striped.$description: Background of every other row of a striped data table.

table.$comment-changed: A changed value's flash starts on the warning's second fill and fades to the row's surface: the colour a reading that moved is caught in, not a warning of anything. The second fill and not the first, which the warning tone wears, or a flash on a warning row would fade from its own colour to itself.

bg-changed.$description: Background a data table's cell flashes in when its value changes.

table.$comment-tones: The four tones a row or a cell wears: each tone's quietest fill and the text paired with it (`on-<tone>-100`), the pair the palette already measures, so a toned row keeps the contrast of its words.

bg-success.$description: Background of a data table's row or cell in the success tone.

fg-success.$description: Text colour of a data table's row or cell in the success tone.

bg-warning.$description: Background of a data table's row or cell in the warning tone.

fg-warning.$description: Text colour of a data table's row or cell in the warning tone.

bg-danger.$description: Background of a data table's row or cell in the danger tone.

fg-danger.$description: Text colour of a data table's row or cell in the danger tone.

bg-info.$description: Background of a data table's row or cell in the info tone.

fg-info.$description: Text colour of a data table's row or cell in the info tone.

fg-muted.$description: Text colour of the numbers of a data table's rows.

table.$comment-column-max-width: The widest a column whose cells are cut to one line grows before it cuts: in rem, so a reader who raises the root size widens it with the type.

column-max-width.$description: Maximum width of a data table's column whose cells are cut to one line.

table.$comment-mark: A word the quick filter found: the warning's second fill under its paired text, which shows on every tone's quiet fill. A flash shares the fill for its moment, and the mark's words keep their own colour through it.

mark-bg.$description: Background of a word the quick filter found.

mark-fg.$description: Text colour of a word the quick filter found.

table.$comment-details: A row's details stand on the header's surface, so the line that opened below a row reads as the row's own and not as the next row of data.

details-bg.$description: Background of a data table's details row.

table.$comment-group: A group's heading stands on the primary's quietest fill under its paired text, apart from the header's surface and from the stripes, so a heading reads as a heading in a striped table too. The indent is one step of the spacing scale per level, the same step for a group, a row in it and, later, a node of a tree.

group-bg.$description: Background of a data table's group heading.

group-fg.$description: Text colour of a data table's group heading.

indent.$description: How far a data table indents each level of its groups.
